name: Old television / CRT treatment
summary: A sustained locally rendered CRT treatment with scanlines, temporal noise, curvature and overscan, chroma shift, ghosting, bloom, jitter and tracking disturbance, vignette, and continuous micro-flicker capped at two percent — never a fade approximation.
creativeJobs: place a moment in the past
suggest a mediated or recorded image
add texture to a clean source
qualityChecks: scanlines remain visible without obscuring eyes or text
micro-flicker reads as display energy rather than a fade or flash
scanlines, temporal noise, geometry, ghosting, bloom, sync movement, and vignette persist across the complete duration
tube geometry never exposes black corners
project-export movie is exactly 1920x1080, 30 fps, 120 frames, four seconds, ProRes 422 HQ apch/yuv422p10le, and video-only
the Final Cut parent matches one of the two tested source-resource profiles and keeps a four-second spine extent
previewed and exported movie SHA-256 values match
failureModes: tracking displacement that bends faces or makes titles unreadable
safety: check against the three-flashes-per-second threshold before shipping any flicker

riskGates.basis: The closed renderer caps continuous luma modulation at 0.020 times intensity times flickerStrength, so absolute amplitude cannot exceed two percent and no full-frame opacity event exists.

safetyGates.basis: The production graph accepts only typed 0...1 controls, emits no opacity channel, keeps luma modulation within the fixed two-percent ceiling, and was reviewed across ten sustained four-second renders.

provenance.claim: Final Cut supports connected clips above the primary storyline
a connected clip is a child of the spine asset-clip with lane=1 and a parent-relative offset
ten representative production movies established sustained CRT behavior through frame 119 and exact preview/export artifact parity

Final Cut 12.3 returned the exact FCPXML 1.14 construction over the tested 1920x1080 timing-free/audio-free still source and the tested 1920x1080 30 fps eight-second audio-bearing movie source, each with a four-second spine and one opaque four-second video-only ProRes 422 HQ apch treatment
content should not flash more than three times per second

validation.notes: Validated as a sustained, locally rendered, content-addressed, video-only ProRes 422 HQ apch/yuv422p10le CRT treatment connected above the unchanged source. Project export is restricted to 1920x1080, 30 fps, 120 frames, and four seconds; arbitrary duration/aspect renders are preview-only and refused for project export. Final Cut evidence is further bounded to a tested 1920x1080 timing-free/audio-free still source or a tested 1920x1080, 30 fps, eight-second audio-bearing movie source, each used for a four-second spine extent. Preview and export consume the exact same SHA-256-bound movie. All ten audit cases retained monochrome treatment and scanlines through frame 119 with 120 unique frames; observed global luma range was approximately 1.43–3.49 of 255 and no CRT dropout was observed. This is FrameSmith-regenerable baked output, not the retired native base recipe and not an opacity fade.
